title: Module Review Quiz: Move Semantics & Rvalue References

slides.title: Move Semantics & Rvalue References Overview
slides.prompt: This Module Quiz covers lvalues vs rvalues, rvalue references (&&), move constructors, move assignment operators, std::move, perfect forwarding (std::forward), and Rule of Five in C++ (CPP_249 to CPP_256).

slides.title: Rvalue Reference Syntax (CPP_249)
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator symbol pair used to declare an rvalue reference in C++11.
slides.codeSnippet:
int x = 10;
int___ rref = 20; // Binds to temporary rvalue

slides.title: Lvalue vs Rvalue (CPP_249)
slides.prompt: Which statement correctly describes an 'lvalue' in C++?
options: An expression that refers to a persistent memory location with an identifiable address
A temporary expression that disappears immediately after evaluation
A constant string literal only
A pointer variable allocated dynamically on heap
slides.correctAnswer: An expression that refers to a persistent memory location with an identifiable address

slides.title: std::move Function (CPP_250)
slides.prompt: Fill in the utility function name used to cast an lvalue expression into an rvalue reference.
options: move
forward
cast
transfer

slides.title: std::move Behavior (CPP_250)
slides.prompt: What does calling 'std::move(obj)' actually perform under the hood?
options: It performs an unconditional static cast of obj to an rvalue reference without moving data itself
It immediately deletes the source memory heap buffer
It creates a deep copy of obj and returns it
It locks the memory location to prevent access
slides.correctAnswer: It performs an unconditional static cast of obj to an rvalue reference without moving data itself

slides.title: Move Constructor Signature (CPP_251)
slides.prompt: Fill in the parameter modifier required for a Move Constructor of class 'Widget'.
options: const &

slides.title: Move Constructor Purpose (CPP_251)
slides.prompt: Why are Move Constructors designed to steal resources instead of making deep copies?
options: To eliminate expensive dynamic memory allocations and improve program performance
To enforce immutability on original variables
To convert references into static class members
To make memory allocation compatible with C programs
slides.correctAnswer: To eliminate expensive dynamic memory allocations and improve program performance

slides.title: Move Assignment Operator (CPP_252)
slides.prompt: Fill in the return type and operator declaration for a move assignment operator.
options: operator
move
assign
func

slides.title: noexcept on Move Operations (CPP_253)
slides.prompt: Why should Move Constructors and Move Assignment Operators be marked as 'noexcept'?
options: To allow STL containers (like std::vector) to use move operations during re-allocations safely
To prevent compilation errors when compiling with C++03 standards
To force the compiler to generate inline machine code
To automatically initialize raw pointers to nullptr
slides.correctAnswer: To allow STL containers (like std::vector) to use move operations during re-allocations safely

slides.title: Universal Reference (CPP_254)
slides.prompt: Fill in the template type parameter combination that forms a Universal Reference (Forwarding Reference).
options: const &

slides.title: Perfect Forwarding (CPP_254)
slides.prompt: Which function template works together with universal references to preserve the value category (lvalue/rvalue) of arguments?
options: std::forward<T>()
std::move()
std::cast()
std::pass()

slides.title: Rule of Five (CPP_255)
slides.prompt: Fill in the number of special member functions defined in the C++ 'Rule of Five'.
slides.codeSnippet:
// Destructor, Copy Constructor, Copy Assignment, Move Constructor, Move Assignment
// Rule of ___

slides.title: Rule of Zero (CPP_255)
slides.prompt: What does the 'Rule of Zero' advocate for custom C++ classes?
options: Design classes using smart pointers and standard RAII types so no custom destructors or copy/move operations are needed
Set all class member variable values to zero in constructors
Never define any constructors inside class definitions
Delete all virtual functions from base classes
slides.correctAnswer: Design classes using smart pointers and standard RAII types so no custom destructors or copy/move operations are needed

slides.title: Moved-From State (CPP_256)
slides.prompt: What condition must a source object be left in after its contents have been moved?
options: A valid but unspecified state (safe to destroy or re-assign)
Must be permanently locked and inaccessible
Must throw a runtime error if read
Automatically set to nullptr automatically by C++ runtime
slides.correctAnswer: A valid but unspecified state (safe to destroy or re-assign)
